input.command: git status && git branch -vv && git log -5 --oneline && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null; git merge-base HEAD origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null; git remote -v; ls -la
git log --all --oneline -20; echo '---'; git branch -a; echo '---'; git rev-parse HEAD; git log -1 --format='%P %s'; cat .git/HEAD; ls .git/; git show-ref

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts && node smoke.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log 2>&1; node scratch/check.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/check.log 2>&1; echo "smoke exit: $?"; cat /opt/cursor/artifacts/check.log

cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision> Normalize passing numbers to +digits after dropping an optional leading + or 00, and keep failing input verbatim (empty → null). That matches “standard format so support can call it” plus the fail-open clarification, instead of counting 00 as part of the country code or returning null on every failed check.</risk> Reviewers should confirm 00 is meant as an international prefix (so 001234567 becomes +1234567) and that 16+ digits are stored as typed the same way as short numbers.</verified> Ran `node smoke.ts` (export loads; dummy args throw as expected) and `node scratch/check.ts` (16 cases: 7–15 digit pass, short/long/non-numeric fail-as-typed, +/00 prefixes, empty → null).
EOF
git add impl.ts artifacts && git status && git diff --cached --stat
